title: Deferred prefetch rollforward and catchup: operator playbook
author: Nina Alvarez
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes operator steps, decision thresholds, tooling snippets, and post-recovery checks for handling deferred prefetch windows that require rollforward and catchup processing of KV/prefix caches in the runtime. It is intended for platform operators and oncall engineers running the Redwood inference control plane and platform operator surface.

Problem statement
-----------------
When the runtime defers prefetch work (due to resource constraints, backpressure, or safety cages), cached state (KV/prefix) for models and tenants can lag behind live traffic. If deferred windows grow, operators must reconcile degraded inference quality / higher token cost against capacity and thermal constraints. This playbook provides a safe rollforward/catchup procedure to catch caches up while preserving SLOs and avoiding cascading evictions.

Scope and applicability
----------------------
- Applies to multitenant prefix/KV caches and cross-region prefetch coordinators.
- Intended for cases where deferred prefetch backlog > 5% of steady-state rate OR when tail-latency SLOs show progressive degradation.
- Not intended for full rebuilds after data corruption; see Recovery from corrupt KV index runbook.

Definitions
-----------
- deferred window: period where prefetch worker(s) paused or intentionally delayed work.
- rollforward: operator-driven controlled processing of deferred queue with throttles.
- catchup: continuous incremental rebuild until backlog below target threshold.
- catchup rate: configured fraction of peak prefetch throughput used during catchup.

Prerequisites and safety checks
-------------------------------
1) Confirm data integrity: run kv-checksum --model <model> --shard <id>.
2) Verify operator runway: ensure oncall capacity and cross-team pager coverage for 2 hours.
3) Ensure snapshot retention present for rollback: s3://redwood-prefetch-snapshots/<date>.
4) Confirm capacity cushion: free GPU headroom >= 12% on target pools or have burst credits enabled.

Observability to inspect before starting
--------------------------------------
- SLOs and current burn: dashboards/runtime/slo-summary (look for token latency p95/p99).
- Prefetch backlog: metric prefetch.backlog.count (alert level: > 2000).
- Catchup consumer lag: prefetch.consumer.lag_seconds.
- Token cost delta: cost.tokens.delta_last_1h.
- Thermal and GPU interference: gpu.thermal.high and gpu.interference.score.

Decision matrix (quick)
-----------------------
1) If backlog < 1,000 and p99 latency stable -> schedule low-priority background catchup (dry run).
2) If backlog 1,000–5,000 with p95 rising -> soft rollforward at 10% catchup rate with verification windows.
3) If backlog > 5,000 or p99 > SLO threshold -> escalate and run controlled rollforward with tight throttles and tenant prioritization.
4) If GPU thermal alarms active -> abort rollforward and escalate to infra runbook.

Operator runbook: step-by-step
-----------------------------
1) Notification and coordination
   - Notify impacted owners via #platform-operators and create an incident channel (if not already).
   - Post short summary to status page draft: "Prefetch deferred backlog detected; running controlled catchup".

2) Lock-in safety config
   - Set cluster flag to safe-mode=true: curl -X POST $ADMIN_API/flags/safe-mode -d '{"value":true}'.
   - Annotate deployment with tag rollback-safe:true.

3) Select catchup plan
   - Tiered tenant prioritization table (example):
     | priority | criteria | catchup rate | notes |
     | P0 | enterprise SLA customers | 20% | prefer local shard catchup |
     | P1 | high-value active tenants | 10% | stagger across regions |
     | P2 | best-effort tenants | 5% | throttle aggressively |

4) Execute staged rollforward
   - Start with a canary shard:
     a) Run: prefetchctl start-catchup --shard shard-12 --rate 0.1 --dry-run=false
     b) Watch metrics for 10 minutes: prefetch.backlog.count, latency p95/p99, token cost.
   - If stable, expand to contiguous shards in batches of 4 every 15 minutes.
   - Commands:
     - prefetchctl inspect-backlog --model <model> --shard <shard>
     - prefetchctl start-catchup --shard <shard> --rate <decimal> --owner <team>

5) Adaptive throttling rules
   - If p95 latency increases by > 12% over baseline -> reduce catchup rate by 50% and wait 5 minutes.
   - If GPU utilization > 88% or thermal alarm -> pause catchup immediately and rollback that batch.
   - If token cost delta > 30% and business owner requests -> degrade to P0-only catchup.

6) Monitoring windows and verification
   - Run automated verification suite after each batch:
     - Sample requests for top-10 P0 tenants and run evals against golden prompt set.
     - Verify output similarity score >= acceptance threshold (0.92).
   - Commands:
     - ./tools/eval-sample --tenant <tenant> --prompt-set p0-smoke --expected-score 0.92

7) Completion and cleanup
   - When backlog < 5% of baseline, gradually restore safe-mode=false.
   - Record catchup run in incident log with timestamps, shards acted on, and final metrics.

Rollback playbook (if degradation observed)
-----------------------------------------
1) Pause current batch: prefetchctl pause-catchup --batch <id>.
2) Rollback to last stable snapshot: prefetchctl rollback --shard <shard> --snapshot s3://...
3) Re-open operator channel; call for cross-team mitigation and thermal remediation.

Preflight checklist (operator)
-----------------------------
- [ ] KV checksum passed for targeted shards.
- [ ] Snapshot verified and accessible.
- [ ] Backup plan created with exact rollback commands.
- [ ] Owners and SRE notified and oncall assigned.
- [ ] Observability panels open and annotated.

YAML example: catchup schedule config
-----------------------------------
```yaml
catchup_plan:
  name: staged-rollforward-2026-07
  global_rate_limit: 0.2
  batches:
    - id: batch-1
      shards: [12,13,14,15]
      default_rate: 0.10
      priority_overrides: {p0: 0.20} 
    - id: batch-2
      shards: [16,17,18,19]
      default_rate: 0.08
      priority_overrides: {p0: 0.18}
  telemetry_verification:
    sampling_prompts: p0-smoke
    acceptance_score: 0.92
```

Post-recovery metrics to capture
--------------------------------
- backlog reduction curve (minutes vs backlog count).
- token cost delta and chargeback per tenant.
- latency histogram pre/during/post for top 3 models.
- number of rollbacks and snapshots used.

Automation and tooling notes
--------------------------
- The prefetchctl CLI is the canonical operator surface. For one-off operations use the CLI; for scheduled orchestration use the catchup-controller service which consumes YAML plans.
- Alerts tuned for this procedure:
  - prefetch.catchup.progress.stalled -> alert if no progress for 20 minutes.
  - prefetch.rollforward.error -> immediate P0 notify.

Postmortem template (to fill after run)
-------------------------------------
1) Summary of event and root cause.
2) Timelines: detection, run start, batches, completion.
3) Metrics and impact table.
4) What went well and action items (owner + due date).

Open risks and follow-ups
------------------------
- Need stronger GPU thermal prediction for rollforward windows (action: infra to run thermal forecasting POC).
- Improve tenant scoring to automatically prioritize by latency sensitivity rather than static labels.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary owner: Platform Operators team (pager: platform-operators).
- Secondary: Serving Runtime SRE.
- Escalation: follow the oncall SLO escalation ladder documented in /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/oncall-lagging-telemetry-reconstitution-and-synthetic-backfill-guide-2025.
